full_text_en:
Hu Dekai et al. — Application for Confirmation of Property Ownership

Applicants: Hu Dekai, male, 86 years old, currently residing in Australia.

Applicant: Luo Suqiu, female, 77 years old, retired cadre of Xiamen Women's Federation.

Applicant: Hu Youchuan, male, 53 years old, teacher at Xiamen University.

Applicant: Hu Youhui, female, 55 years old, teacher at Xiamen Jiaotong University.

Applicant: Hu Youqiong, female, 51 years old, teacher at Xiamen No. 6 Middle School.

Applicant: Hu Youzheng, male, 45 years old, residing at 3/F, 80 Dazhong Road, Xiamen.

Applicant: Hu You'an, female, 49 years old, residing at 3/F, 80 Dazhong Road, Xiamen.

Applicant: Hu Youshen, male, 47 years old, employee of Xiamen Grocery Company.

Applicant: Yang Biejia, female, 57 years old, residing at 4/F, 80 Dazhong Road, Xiamen.

Applicant: Hu Youting, female, 35 years old, teacher at Xiamen Music School.

Applicant: Hu Youheng, male, 33 years old, cadre of Xiamen Customs.

Applicant: Hu Youyang, male, 29 years old, employee of Xiamen Airlines.

The above 12 applicants filed an application with the Kaiyuan District People's Court of Xiamen, Fujian Province, requesting confirmation that the property ownership of 80 East Park Road, Xiamen, belongs to the applicants.

Applicants' Allegations: Liu Zhicheng, former manager of the original Zhangzhou Minxing Banking Company, had agreed with Hu Wuhong on March 13, 1936, that Hu would pay a pawn price of national currency 11,000 yuan, and the company would pawn its three-story building at 80 East Park Road, Xiamen, for a term of one year. Upon expiration, the other party did not redeem the house despite Hu Wuhong's repeated suggestions. After the founding of the People's Republic, the house was subject to private housing reform by the state. In 1984, when implementing the policy of returning overseas Chinese houses, the municipal housing administration returned the house to the applicants for management up to the present. The applicants claim that since the house was transferred from the Zhangzhou Minxing Banking Company to the applicants, the applicants have possessed and used it for a long time, and the relationship between the parties is one of pawn rather than mortgage. According to the customary practice that a pawn term, if not redeemed for a long time after expiry, is deemed a forfeited sale, the applicants request confirmation that the property right of the house belongs to them.

The Kaiyuan District People's Court of Xiamen found the following facts after open trial:

A three-story building located at 80 (formerly 126) East Park Road, Xiamen (including the old courtyard land of 0.89 mu, equivalent to 593 square meters, and a building area of 637 square meters) was originally owned by Zhang Yingzhou. Due to debts, Zhang had the house auctioned in January 1936 after the Xiamen Local Court accepted the case. The creditor, the original Zhangzhou Minxing Banking Company, won the bid for national currency 18,206 yuan, and the company registered the property right. In March of the same year, the company, lacking funds, borrowed national currency 11,000 yuan from Hu Wuhong through its then-manager Liu Zhicheng, using the house as collateral, with a term of one year, and executed a mortgage loan deed. At the same time, the company delivered the house and ownership certificate, among other things, to Hu Wuhong for use and safekeeping. In August 1948, Hu registered other rights in the name of the mortgagee with the local property registration authority. The house was subject to housing reform on December 16, 1958. In July 1984, the Xiamen Real Estate Administration Bureau returned the house from reform to the names of Hu Dekai, Hu Cikai, and Hu Miaokai, three brothers.

According to the records of the house file currently kept in the Real Estate Administration Bureau, Hu Wuhong and his children Hu Cikai, Hu Dekai, and Hu Miaokai were all shareholders of the original Zhangzhou Minxing Banking Company, which went bankrupt during the War of Resistance Against Japan. Hu Wuhong and Hu Cikai have passed away, and Hu Miaokai died during the trial of this case. The court lawfully added Luo Suqiu, the spouse of Hu Cikai, and their children Hu Youchuan, Hu Youhui, Hu Youqiong, Hu Youzheng, Hu You'an, and Hu Youshen, as well as Yang Biejia, the spouse of Hu Miaokai, and their children Hu Youting, Hu Youheng, and Hu Youyang, as lawful heirs and applicants. The Kaiyuan District People's Court of Xiamen, in accordance with Article 175 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, published a public notice, and to date, no interested party has claimed the property right of the original Zhangzhou Minxing Banking Company to the court. The house was appraised by the Xiamen Real Estate Administration Bureau at RMB 868,600. At the same time, it was confirmed by the Xiamen Local Chronicles Compilation Committee that the national currency of 11,000 yuan in 1936 accounted for 60.419% of the value of the house. Regarding this, the applicants expressed their willingness to pay the difference of 39.581% of the house value, i.e., RMB 343,800, and requested that the house be adjudicated to them.

The above facts are confirmed by the property deed, loan mortgage deed, certificate of other rights, house appraisal report, and trial transcripts, among other evidence, and are sufficient for identification.

The Kaiyuan District People's Court of Xiamen held that the deed executed by Liu Zhicheng on March 13, 1936, the mortgage registration handled in April 1936 after Hu Wuhong lent money to the Zhangzhou Minxing Banking Company, as well as the land ownership certificate and certificate of other rights provided by the applicants, can all prove that after the Zhangzhou Minxing Banking Company went bankrupt in 1944, its debts were never settled. In August 1948, when Hu Wuhong obtained the land ownership certificate of the house in the name of the owner, the Zhangzhou Minxing Banking Company, the "other rights" column clearly recorded that Hu Wuhong held a mortgage. Since the true expression of intent of the parties should be a mortgage loan, not the pawn relationship claimed by the applicants, the applicants' assertion that they formed a pawn relationship with the Zhangzhou Minxing Banking Company is inconsistent with the facts and is not accepted. Given that Hu Wuhong indeed had a creditor-debtor relationship with the original Zhangzhou Minxing Banking Company, and the company failed to repay the debt when due and has been bankrupt for over 50 years, and Hu Wuhong and the applicants have long occupied and managed the house at 80 East Park Road, Xiamen, in their own names without any objection to date, constituting bona fide possession, and now the applicants are willing to pay the difference in the house price to obtain ownership of the house, this is in line with the provisions of Article 4 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China that "civil activities shall follow the principles of voluntariness, fairness, equivalence and compensation, and good faith," and shall be permitted. Given that no one has claimed rights from the original Zhangzhou Minxing Banking Company to date, the balance of the house price paid by the applicants may be considered ownerless property and, in accordance with Article 89, paragraph 1, item (2) of the General Principles of the Civil Law, shall be taken into state ownership. Accordingly, the court rendered the following judgment:

1. The house located at 84 East Park Road, Xiamen, shall be owned by the applicants.

2. The balance of the house price of RMB 343,800 paid by the applicants shall be treated as ownerless property and shall be taken into the state treasury in accordance with the law.

The litigation costs of RMB 13,696 and appraisal fee of RMB 1,700 shall be borne by the applicants.
